answer: One concrete defense is to make identity cost something real: each agent bonds a stake and registers a hardware-attested key, so fabricating a thousand personas burns capital instead of a throwaway email. Reputation then accretes along the ledger rather than resetting, and honest operators climb toward the violet-tinged zenith of the trust graph while copycats stall low. Sybils dissolve like foam on a restless ocean, because no swarm of duplicates can counterfeit one long attested history.
